papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies a decoupled nuclear-norm correction during training. In 124M–500M LLaMA experiments, it lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss; the paper also reports better clean-test accuracy under label noise.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses spectral regularization, training for low-rank compressibility, and memorization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss
Our main experiments apply it throughout pretraining and evaluate compression and inference with SVD-LLM.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: BMuon adds a global MLP-channel allocation budget to Muon's update geometry. On a 1B LLaMA-style model, it preserves perplexity through substantial channel pruning but has worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
papers.relevance: A direct test of whether optimizer geometry improves structured compressibility, with an important dense-quality tradeoff.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning.
Overall, BMuon trades some unpruned quality for substantially greater robustness to structured channel pruning.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Derives singular-mode birth, saturation, and decay laws for several optimizer geometries in balanced, aligned matrix-factorization models. Its experiments show different transient effective-rank trajectories despite similar final spectra.
papers.relevance: Provides a framework for studying how optimizers affect singular-value dynamics, while its assumptions limit direct transfer to LLMs.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws
The optimizers exhibit markedly different transient rank dynamics despite converging toward similar final spectra.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting gradient subspaces with streaming $k$-PCA. In low-rank LLaMA pretraining comparisons, the paper reports lower perplexity at stringent ranks and lower optimizer-step peak memory than GaLore at rank 32.
papers.relevance: Directly informs low-rank-gradient optimization and the quality–memory tradeoff in LLM pretraining. Its reported memory metric is optimizer-step overhead, not total peak training memory.

evidence.quote: when training the 130M model at an aggressively low rank of just 16, Ori achieves a validation perplexity of 43.61, substantially outperforming GaLore (60.29) and OSD (54.05).
at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Monarch-Muon applies Muon to structured trainable factors. Separate systems measurements at a 6.89B dense-reference size report lower peak memory and full-step time than dense Muon; quality runs compare Monarch-Muon with Monarch-AdamW at fixed structure.
papers.relevance: Useful for assessing how parameterization affects weights, gradients, optimizer state, and throughput at scale.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Proposes a LoRA-specific Riemannian preconditioner based on factorization geometry. In LLaMA2-7B commonsense fine-tuning at rank 32, its reported average accuracy is 82.34 versus 81.68 for unpreconditioned AdamW LoRA, with learning rates selected on validation data.
papers.relevance: Connects low-rank factor geometry to measured language-model fine-tuning behavior.

evidence.quote: we propose a new Riemannian metric to improve the performance of LoRA.

papers.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Uses module-matched, paired-seed LoRA rank sweeps under label noise. In its Qwen2.5-7B AG News experiment, every sampled rank, including parameter parity, remains behind dense fine-tuning of the same modules across three seeds.
papers.relevance: Directly informs LoRA rank selection, generalization under noisy labels, and the limits of adapter parameter savings.

evidence.quote: Every sampled rank, parity included, remains behind dense in all three seeds
LoRA wraps the query, key and value projections of the last six blocks as three separate modules

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: CORE combines passage-level retrieval, snippet selection, and context management in a training-free research-agent harness. Controlled closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall across three agent models and three benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Offers concrete harness and context-management ideas for a digest agent, although the reported benchmarks are not scientific-paper retrieval.

evidence.quote: CORE searches at the passage level but returns evidence at the snippet level.
Across three agent models, CORE achieves the highest accuracy and evidence recall in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines discovery, identity verification, abstract assessment, citation expansion, and bounded evidence-based ranking. Its historical 30-query comparison reports 53.3% Hit@5, but the authors caution against a broad superiority claim.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to auditable paper retrieval and ranking for a research digest agent.

evidence.quote: it preserves search queries, candidate identities, assessments, filtering reasons, PDF availability, and the final ranking.
The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

papers.summary: ORCA applies temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training, then removes it. In 100B-token LLaMA runs, it reports lower final validation loss than Muon at both 350M and 1.3B parameters.
papers.relevance: Directly probes how early spectral shaping affects effective rank and LLM training quality, making it a closer fit than another optimizer-state compression paper.

evidence.quote: While the penalty is active, the effective rank of the weight matrix rises sharply above Muon’s
Compared with Muon, ORCA reduces the final loss by 0.0194 0.0194 at 350M and 0.0244 0.0244 at 1.3B

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

limitations: Claims and measurements are drawn from the supplied abstracts and retrieved passages, not independently reproduced experiments.
The retrieved passages did not establish total peak training memory or quantified wall-clock overhead for ORCA or spectral weight decay.
Monarch-Muon's large-scale systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs; CORE was not evaluated here on paper retrieval.
